reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that helping the Hebrew people (Israelites) is one of Yahweh's central goals. Yahweh states to Moses that He will bring one final plague upon Egypt and then release the Israelites ('יְשַׁלַּח אֶתְכֶם' - 'he will let you go'). Throughout the passage, Yahweh actively protects the Israelites from the plagues—no harm comes to them while Egypt suffers the death of the firstborn. The text explicitly states that Yahweh distinguishes between Egypt and Israel ('יַפְלֶה יְהוָה בֵּין מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל'). Additionally, Yahweh grants the Hebrew people favor with the Egyptians, enabling them to receive gifts of silver, gold, and clothing. The passage culminates with the successful departure of the Israelites from Egypt—the concrete fulfillment of Yahweh's stated objective. These multiple coordinated actions directly evidence that liberating and assisting the Hebrew people is indeed one of Yahweh's primary goals in this narrative.
